html:
Brazil was ruled by its armed forces from the coup of 1 April 1964, which overthrew President João Goulart, until a civilian took office in March 1985.

The army, backed by the United States and much of the middle class, feared Goulart's plans for land reform. Generals ruled in turn, with a tame Congress. From 1968 the regime closed Congress for a time, censored the press and tortured opponents; hundreds were killed or disappeared, and thousands went into exile, among them the musicians of the bossa nova and Tropicália.

The years 1968 to 1973 brought the economic miracle, with fast growth, the Trans-Amazonian Highway and the Itaipu Dam, paid for by foreign debt. After the oil shocks, debt and inflation soared. A slow opening, an amnesty in 1979 and mass protests for direct elections led to civilian rule. Brazil took part in Operation Condor.
sum: Brazil was ruled by its armed forces from the coup of 1 April 1964, which overthrew President João Goulart, until a civilian took office in March 1985.
